$comment2: Do not add short or generic literals to `webview`/`extension`. "(optional)" was tried and rejected: it also occurs inside the bundled TextMate grammars for Clarity and Fortran, where it is documentation, not UI.
$comment: Strings that the language pack mechanism cannot reach, for the optional installation patcher
(`npm run patch`). Everything here is applied by rewriting files inside the installed Kiro,
which is unsupported by definition: a Kiro update overwrites them. Nothing in this file affects
manifest   values in extensions/kiro.kiro-agent/package.json that carry no %key% indirection
(inline values without %key% indirection). Replaced structurally: only known
localizable fields are considered, so an English word here cannot leak into an id.
extension  literals in dist/extension.js. Runtime strings that would be translatable through
vscode.l10n.t() if Kiro called it. Keep these long and unambiguous.
webview    literals in packages/*/dist/**/*.js - the React chat UI. Same rule.
Rules: keep {0} placeholders, $(codicon) markers and (command:...) targets exactly as they are.
For extension/webview entries the English side must match the source byte for byte, including
punctuation, and must be specific enough not to appear anywhere else.
